title: Where the project stands on 17 November, and the steps that remain
subtitle:
Stages A to D have run and all 360 Stage D cells are in. Intervals are 95% t-intervals over the five scaffold splits, not adjusted for the number of comparisons.
ESOL is scored by RMSE (lower is better), BBBP by AUROC (higher is better). "Untrained" is the same network fine-tuned from a random start.

done.heading: DONE: what each stage showed, and how we read it

cards.head: Stage A: the corpora
cards.body: The corpora differ, by up to 2.15 SD on a single property. PubChem is the nearest to both benchmarks, COCONUT next, both ZINC arms far. PubChem already contains 73% of BBBP and 93% of ESOL.
cards.reading: Composition had room to matter, and benchmark exposure had to be controlled.

cards.head: Stage B: the yardsticks
cards.body: One fine-tuning path for every encoder, and three baselines. The released encoder beats the untrained one on ESOL, −0.228 [−0.439, −0.018]. On BBBP, no link detected between a molecule's nearness to the corpus and its gain.
cards.reading: The recipe transfers. Where the gain lives is still open.

cards.head: Stage C: corpus size
cards.body: ESOL at full labels, against the untrained encoder: no separable gain below 25,000 molecules; −0.106 [−0.190, −0.023] at 25,000; going on to 100,000 adds −0.017 [−0.064, +0.030]. BBBP: no size separates. A benchmark-free encoder is not told apart from a second seed.
cards.reading: Size matters up to about 25,000 molecules on ESOL. Past that we see nothing more.

cards.head: Stage D: composition
cards.body: At 25,000 molecules, ZINC general, ZINC NP-like and COCONUT are not told apart. 2 of the 6 registered intervals exclude zero, each by about 0.001, and none once the 6 are taken together. Two seeds of one corpus differ by more (0.044 RMSE) than two corpora do (0.036).
cards.reading: A null with wide intervals. Stage D could only have seen a difference of about 0.06 RMSE or more.

cards.head: Across the stages
cards.body: Chemprop given computed descriptors, with no pretraining, reaches 0.792 RMSE on ESOL at full labels. The PubChem 25,000 encoders of Stage C reach 0.837, the three Stage D corpora 0.863 to 0.900, the untrained encoder 0.944.
cards.reading: No encoder we pretrained is separably better than that baseline, in any cell.
